657.body:
Fixes #646

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

**Label note.** `agent-ready` could not be applied from this account (403 with both REST and the connector, same as #641); this PR is proposed ahead of the 24 h label window because of the owner's sprint deadline. Claim record: issue comment `6486721604`.

## What the problem is

`putWorkspaceFile` re-derived the source digest and then re-read the stored object on every cache hit, so one hit cost two full reads (`unchangedWorkspaceBytes` → `verifyRef`). At 1 MiB that was 9.404 ms median, with the two halves costing the same (source hash 4.591 ms, object hash 4.682 ms): the cost is SHA-256 throughput, not syscall overhead. `services/runner/src/execution-manager.ts:96` snapshots the workspace after every shell execution, so it was paid per execution.

The source re-hash stays. It is the only criterion that survives a same-size in-place rewrite inside one filesystem timestamp tick — that is #641, where metadata-based reuse served stale bytes in 171 of 200 iterations. The object read is the removable half: the object is content-addressed, written once through `link` + `fsync`, and this store already records what it verified in `admitted`, whose entries `checked` revokes on any integrity failure.

## Trust boundary

A `VersionStore` instance verifies a stored object once and then admits it; the source bytes are still re-hashed on every reuse, so a same-size in-place rewrite of the workspace file is still caught. An admission is evidence that *this instance* saw those bytes, not that they are still the verified ones. The admission assumes no writer outside this process changes an object after this process verified it — the same assumption `validateClosureForCommit` has relied on since before this change. Every path that hands bytes to a caller re-hashes and fails closed (`Object integrity failure`), so a tampered or vanished object can never be delivered as good data; a vanished object makes the next cache hit republish it.

Attribution, so this is not read as a regression: `admitted`, and `validateClosureForCommit` skipping already-admitted objects, are pre-existing. #642 brought the source re-hash on reuse, the object verification, and `checked()` clearing admissions. This PR changes exactly one thing: `unchangedWorkspaceBytes` no longer calls `verifyRef` for an already-admitted ref (`packages/cas/src/versioning.ts:146-152`), turning per-reuse verification into per-instance verification, with the #641 fix untouched. A size/mtime shortcut was deliberately not added, and the admission was deliberately not narrowed to a single snapshot or put sequence: the first would reopen the blind spot #642 closed, the second would remove the benefit this PR exists for.

Known limitation, deliberately kept: an admission means only that this instance saw those bytes. Existence is re-checked on every admitted read; content is not. A same-size, same-mtime replacement of an *object* is therefore not detected by the admission itself, and surfaces only as a fail-closed error (`ENOENT` or `Object integrity failure`) at the next read, audit or new-instance rehash that touches those bytes. On the commit path (`validateReachable` with `trustAdmitted`, used by `validateClosureForCommit`) an admitted record is stopped at that existence check: its bytes, and the closure behind them, are not re-read, so a replaced-but-present record is accepted by the commit and fails closed only when something later calls `read` / `readRecord` / `validateClosure` on it. That skip of already-admitted objects is pre-existing — this PR only puts the existence check in front of it. The admission can never make a tampered object be delivered as good data.

## Commits

- `1889093442a7db831c2a22c2932df2387fe0c063` — the red test only: `a cache hit does not re-read the stored object on every call`.
- `f54ef875a78db25f58ad294528b83badf04d4d17` — the fix: admit the object after its first successful `verifyRef` and skip the re-read afterwards (one verification per object per store instance), and document that in `putWorkspaceFile`/`unchangedWorkspaceBytes`.
- `32c45733f7b083c2a3fccaef0cf45670513e4f86` — follow-up to the reviewer finding: a cache hit `stat`s the admitted object before trusting the admission, so a blob that disappeared under a live process falls back to the existing `return undefined` → republish path, plus the regression test for it.

- `da2036e653c1907759816d885405a37885db61f1` — red tests for the second admitted reader: the fail-closed read assertion in the republish case, and a case where an admitted root is removed before the next ref commit.
- `37fb64bdbf673e2b187a3d9aef3883741e2a5075` — the fix for it: one shared `dropIfVanished` helper, called before trusting an admission in **both** readers.

All five commits are on the head branch, in order, each on top of its predecessor; `git fetch` of a bare SHA needs the fork remote or `refs/pull/657/head`. No amend, no force-push.

## Red → green

```bash
cd packages/cas
node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "cache hit does not re-read" src/versioning.test.ts
```

Before (`a074172f` + the red-test commit):

```
  error: |-
    the stored object is verified once per store instance, not once per cache hit

  expected: 1
  actual: 2
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

After (this tip):

```
# pass 1
# fail 0
```

The test also rewrites the file in place afterwards and asserts a new digest is published, so the source re-hash cannot be traded away for the object cache.

Second pair, for the commit path (`da2036e6` red, `37fb64bd` green):

```bash
cd packages/cas
node --import tsx --test src/versioning.test.ts
```

Before (`32c45733` + the red test commit): **18 tests, 17 pass, 1 fail**

```
# Subtest: a ref commit re-verifies an admitted object that disappeared instead of trusting the admission
not ok 18 - a ref commit re-verifies an admitted object that disappeared instead of trusting the admission
  error: 'Missing expected rejection.'
  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
# pass 17
# fail 1
```

After (this tip): **18 tests, 18 pass, 0 fail** in that file, and `src/**/*.test.ts` is **39/39 pass, 0 fail**.

## Cost, measured

Harness: node v22.23.2, single thread, ext4, page-cache warm, 25 iterations after 3 warm-ups, one `putWorkspaceFile` cache hit, median / max in ms.

| file | before (`a074172f`) | after (this tip) | source-hash-only lower bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 KiB | 1.202 / 2.225 | 0.617 / 1.467 | 0.596 / 0.788 |
| 1 MiB | 9.404 / 11.050 | 4.748 / 5.339 | 4.701 / 5.167 |
| 8 MiB | 68.317 / 71.872 | 34.062 / 35.194 | 34.103 / 48.020 |

After the fix the hit cost sits on the source hash, i.e. the second read is gone. Aggregate through the real `snapshotWorkspace` on a 64 × 1 MiB workspace, all hits: **588.4 ms → 309.4 ms**. A repeat run on a loaded machine inflated both the after column and the source-only bound by the same factor (9.06 / 9.10 ms at 1 MiB), which is the expected shape when only one read remains.

## Review finding: an admission outlived its object

`sciencediscovery-bot` (review `5692570203`, inline `4408458539`, `versioning.ts:147`, Medium) showed that the admission turned "verified on every hit" into "verified once per process": if the blob disappears while the process lives, the next cache hit reuses the ref instead of republishing, and a record can be committed pointing at a missing object.

Reproduced on `f54ef875` and on `a074172f` with the same probe (put → put → `rm` blob → put → `readData`):

| step | `a074172f` | `f54ef875` |
|---|---|---|
| `BLOB_RESTORED` after the third put | `true` | `false` |
| `readData(ref)` | `OK` | `ENOENT` |

Fix: before trusting an admission, `stat` the object (`ENOENT` → the existing `return undefined` → republish branch). One syscall against a source re-hash that is milliseconds per hit. Regression test: `a cache hit republishes a stored object that disappeared after its first verification` — red on `f54ef875` (`expected: true / actual: false` at the post-republish `existsSync`), green after the `stat`.

Security follow-up (same review, wider scope): the existence check was only on the put path, while `admitted` has two readers — `unchangedWorkspaceBytes` and `validateReachable` (used by `validateClosureForCommit`). Removing an already-admitted record and committing without an intervening put therefore still produced a version that pointed at missing bytes. `dropIfVanished` is now shared by both, uses `lstat` + `isFile()` so an object replaced by a directory or a symlink is treated the same as a missing one, and revokes every admission exactly like `checked()` does; the commit path then reaches `readRecord`/`verifyRef`, which throws `ENOENT`. The helper is existence evidence only — it never claims the bytes are still the verified ones. Scope, so this is not read as a rewrite: `validateReachable` already skipped admitted objects on `main`, so the gap was pre-existing; this PR adds one `dropIfVanished` call at that reader rather than restructuring it. Still out of scope, as directed: a vanished *transitive dependency* of an admitted record (a different change), and any size/mtime shortcut.

## Validation

Ran:
- `cd packages/cas && node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"` on this tip: **39/39 pass, 0 fail**.
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p packages/cas/tsconfig.json` and `--noEmit`: exit 0.
- The red test on `a074172f` + the first commit (output above).

Not run locally:
- repository-wide layers (`ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e`): the pnpm wrapper aborts with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY` in this container; this PR's own CI run is the authority for those.

## Release

`release:fix` — label to be applied by a maintainer (labels are not writable from this account, 403).

Fixes #651

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

**Label note.** `agent-ready` could not be applied from this account (403 with both REST and the connector, same as #641/#646); this PR is proposed ahead of the 24 h label window because of the owner's sprint deadline. Claim record: Lead's pickup-ok on #651 — issue comment 6487338598.

The function's own comment already states the invariant: a shape with no row/column mapping must be shown as JSON text.

## What changes

- After the shape filter, require at least one key across the records: `records.some((record) => Object.keys(record).length > 0)`.
- `[{}, {}]` and `[{}]` now route to `json-source` (re-indented document); record arrays with keys keep the table unchanged.
- Single file, no schema change.

## Commits

- `ffea066d0dc58dd74fe49e4949c04b0861e84f6f` — the red tests only: empty-object arrays must render as JSON text, and record arrays with keys must keep the table.

- `a json artifact of empty objects renders as JSON text, not an empty grid` — `[{}, {}]` and `[{}]` must be `json-source` with `source === JSON.stringify(records, null, 2)`.

663.author: HugoXK
663.body:
Fixes #660

- Owner: Dev1
- Written-by: Dev-1
- Base: `a074172f60e5667e72ff04246316a0a41552cb46` (live `main` when the branch was cut)
- Claim record: pickup-ok `6487423422` named Dev-2; the Lead's append-only reassignment `6487508566` records `#660` as Dev-1 on `dev1/fix/660-truncate-code-point`. No `dev2/fix/660-*` branch or PR ever existed.
- `agent-ready` is not on this issue (the fork cannot apply labels, HTTP 403), so this PR is opened ahead of the 24h label window under the owner's deadline.

## Red first — `b6a87d12` (tests only)

Five tests in `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts`. The artifact content is `"a".repeat(9) + "\u{1F600}" + "tail"` — 9 ASCII characters, then U+1F600 (two UTF-16 units), then `tail` — previewed with `maxChars = "10"`, so a code-unit cut lands between the two halves of the emoji.

1. `markdown preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair` (`markdown-source`)
2. `latex preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair` (`latex-source`)
3. `structure preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair` (`structure-source`)
4. `json-source preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair` (`json-source`, i.e. the `jsonSourceOf` path shared with `rawJson`)
5. `an ascii markdown preview still cuts at exactly maxChars` — pure ASCII must keep today's result byte for byte (`"x".repeat(10)` from 20), the guard against a code-point rewrite quietly changing ordinary text.

Each surrogate test asserts the payload `source` contains no lone surrogate (the issue's regex, `[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])|(?<![\uD800-\uDBFF])[\uDC00-\uDFFF]`) and that the cut sits on a character boundary — the whole U+1F600 is kept or dropped, never half. `totalChars` / `truncated` keep their current meaning and are asserted unchanged.

```console
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern="surrogate pair|ascii markdown preview" src/dashboard.test.ts
not ok 1 - markdown preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair
    source carries a lone surrogate: "aaaaaaaaa\ud83d"
not ok 2 - latex preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair
    source carries a lone surrogate: "aaaaaaaaa\ud83d"
not ok 3 - structure preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair
    source carries a lone surrogate: "aaaaaaaaa\ud83d"
not ok 4 - json-source preview truncation never splits a surrogate pair
    source carries a lone surrogate: "aaaaaaaaa\ud83d"
ok 5 - an ascii markdown preview still cuts at exactly maxChars
# tests 5
# pass 1
# fail 4
```

Every failing payload ends in `\ud83d`, an unpaired high surrogate: invalid UTF-16 that only the web renderer's one path patches (`SourcePreview.tsx:62` strips a trailing high surrogate), while `json-source`, `structure-source` and the raw-JSON view get no guard.

## Fix — `57146c51`

One helper, called by all four truncating paths:

```ts
function truncateAtCodePoint(text: string, maxChars: number): string {
  if (text.length <= maxChars) return text;
  const last = text.charCodeAt(maxChars - 1);
  const next = text.charCodeAt(maxChars);
  const splitsPair = last >= 0xd800 && last <= 0xdbff && next >= 0xdc00 && next <= 0xdfff;
  return text.slice(0, splitsPair ? maxChars - 1 : maxChars);
}
```

Call sites: markdown (`:465`), latex (`:477`), structure (`:521`) and `jsonSourceOf` (`:322`). A character that would straddle the cut is dropped whole, so `source.length <= maxChars` still holds and `totalChars` / `truncated` keep their existing code-unit meaning — the structure flag (`charTruncated || atomTruncated`) is untouched, and `#659`'s flag change stays Dev-2's PR.

```console
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts
# tests 36
# pass 36
# fail 0

$ node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit
$ echo $?
0
```

## Ran / Not run

- Ran: `node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts` → 36/36; targeted pattern → 5/5; `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → exit 0.
- Not run: repo-wide `pnpm` pipelines (one module and its tests); CI covers UT/ST/E2E on this tip.

## Out of scope

- `#659` / `#655`: the structure truncation flag — different hunk, Dev-2's PR.
- `apps/web/src/SourcePreview.tsx:62`: the web-layer clipping patch; a separate issue if it is to be replaced by trusting the API.

664.author: HugoXK
664.body:
Fixes #662

Owner: Dev2 / Written-by: Dev-2

**Label note.** `agent-ready` could not be applied from this account (403); this PR is proposed ahead of the 24 h label window because of the owner's sprint deadline. Claim record: Lead's pickup-ok on #662 — issue comment 6487523184.

## The defect

`ipv6Blocked` (`packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts:58-69`) extracted an embedded IPv4 only from a dotted-quad tail. IPv4-mapped and IPv4-compatible IPv6 literals written in hex carry no dots, so they fell through to `return false`; `isBlockedAddress` then reported them as public and `assertPublicUrl` accepted them. `web_fetch` takes a model-supplied URL, so this is the SSRF gate itself, not a downstream check.

## What changes

- Expand the IPv6 literal to its eight hextets (compressed `::` and full form both).
- When the address is IPv4-mapped (80 zero bits, then `ffff`) or IPv4-compatible (96 zero bits), rebuild the dotted quad from the last two hextets and hand it to the existing `ipv4Blocked`.
- `ipv4Blocked` and the existing dotted-quad path are untouched; public IPv6 keeps being accepted.

## Commits

- `b9a10c6b1aac5554c6382bee030156f335de871e` — red tests for the hex mapped/compatible literals and the reverse direction.
- `b3d6112fbb228f3787816a6014f0410882b9240d` — red tests for delegation to the existing IPv4 range table and for the resolver path.
- `fc803262da45092ccc184bc27f9c38c9569db00a` — the guard change above.

No amend, no force-push.

## Tests

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/providers.test.ts`:

- `web_fetch judges IPv4-mapped and IPv4-compatible IPv6 literals by their embedded IPv4` — hex mapped and compatible literals are blocked, including the full eight-hextet spelling; the gate rejects them; the dotted-quad path keeps its behaviour.
- Reverse direction in the same test: public mapped and compatible forms stay unblocked and the gate still accepts them, so the change cannot become an over-block.
- Delegation in the same test: embedded addresses outside the `127/10/192.168` prefixes (carrier-grade NAT, benchmarking) are blocked, proving the judgement is delegated to the existing IPv4 range table rather than re-implemented.
- `web_fetch applies the same judgement to resolved addresses, not only literals` — a resolver returning a mapped literal must reject, so the DNS path stays covered.

Before (red-test commits, on `a074172f`):

```
not ok 1 - web_fetch judges IPv4-mapped and IPv4-compatible IPv6 literals by their embedded IPv4
  error: |-
    false !== true
# pass 0
# fail 1

not ok 2 - web_fetch applies the same judgement to resolved addresses, not only literals
  error: 'Missing expected rejection (PublicUrlError).'
# pass 0
# fail 2
```

After (fix commit):

```
# tests 15
# pass 15
# fail 0
```

## Out of scope

The guard still does not decode embedded IPv4 from NAT64 (`64:ff9b::/96` and `64:ff9b:1::/48`), 6to4 (`2002::/16`), Teredo (`2001::/32`), the IPv4-translated range (`::ffff:0:0:0/96`) or the deprecated site-local range (`fec0::/10`). Those are a separate next fix; this PR does not claim the gate is fully closed.

What this change closes: the two spellings that need no translator to reach a target, namely IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:a.b.c.d` in hex) and IPv4-compatible (`::a.b.c.d` in hex), on both the literal path and the resolved-address path. What it does not close: any address family that only reaches a target through a gateway or translator, listed above. Keeping the judgement delegated to the existing IPv4 range table is what makes the next fix a decoder addition rather than a second policy.

## Validation

Ran:
- `cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/web/native/providers.test.ts` — **15/15 pass, 0 fail**.
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.

Not run locally: repository-wide layers (`ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e`), because the pnpm wrapper aborts with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY` in this container; this PR's own CI run is the authority for those.

667.author: qingkwl
667.body:
Closes #666

## Summary

Imports the Windows desktop shell as a new top-level `win_desktop/` directory — an Electron 37 application that owns the backend stack lifecycle, drives the assisted first-run wizard, loads the web UI with the local access token injected, and packages the backend tree into a per-user NSIS installer.

- **Standalone workspace**: own `pnpm-workspace.yaml` + lockfile. The root workspace globs (`config`, `apps/*`, `services/*`, `packages/*`) do not match `win_desktop/`, so root-level workspace behavior is untouched; the one dependency patch (`app-builder-lib@26.15.3`, NSIS progress presentation) is confined to `win_desktop/patches/`.
- **src/** — main process; wizard (data-dir choice: warn at 180 path chars, block past 240, mirrored for the uninstaller); stack orchestration + bootstrap (payload path substitution, venv preparation); bind-probing port epochs; token-injecting proxy + preload; loading stage with heartbeat mapping; window state; retry helpers.
- **test/** — 14 `node:test` suites, no Electron launch required.
- **scripts/** — esbuild build, dev runner, `assemble-backend.mjs` (stages this repo's backend into `build/resources` — `--repo` overrides — rewrites venv trampolines to the install layout, compiles the payload), icon generator.
- **build/** — NSIS include (plain-release presentation, install diagnostics into `$INSTDIR\logs`, clean-uninstall options, silent-never-deletes), uninstall helper (C# + PowerShell long-path removal), license, icons.

## Verification (Windows 11 23H2, Node v24.21.0)

- `pnpm -C win_desktop install` — clean; the `app-builder-lib` patch applies.
- `pnpm -C win_desktop typecheck` — exit 0.
- `pnpm -C win_desktop test` — **113/113 pass** across the 14 suites.

## Merge order

The shell compiles and tests standalone, but assembling a full installer payload stages `scripts/start-stack.mjs` / `scripts/jiuwenswarm.mjs` / `scripts/lib/stack-platform.mjs`, which arrive with the runtime PR (#644). Suggested order: #640 → #644 → this one. No file overlap with either — this PR only adds the new `win_desktop/` tree.

## Risks

- Windows-only toolchain (Electron, electron-builder, NSIS): nothing here runs in the Linux CI today; evidence is real-machine (same gap as #639/#643).
- The `app-builder-lib` patch pins NSIS progress behavior — an electron-builder major bump will need the patch re-evaluated.
- No auto-update channel yet; the payload layout is blockmap-friendly so one can be added later without repackaging.
